title: MatToolBench: Benchmarking Multimodal Agents in Real-World Materials Science Workflows
abstract: Multimodal GUI agents have achieved impressive results on general software benchmarks, yet their ability to operate professional scientific software remains largely unexplored. In materials science, sparse domain-specific web data, specialized interfaces, and tacit workflow conventions create blind spots that general-purpose pretraining cannot readily bridge. We present MatToolBench, the first real-environment benchmark for evaluating multimodal GUI agents on professional materials science software, comprising 204 tasks across 10 tools in three modalities: GUI operation, OriginPro scripting, and code-based database queries, all executed inside a Windows 11 VM. Each task is decomposed into fine-grained sub-criteria by domain experts, enabling interpretable partial-credit scoring; the GUI component of our multi-level evaluation pipeline achieves an average F1 of 0.98. For OriginPro figure-generation tasks, we further conduct a human-LLM agreement study to validate the use of a multimodal judge for secondary aesthetic assessment. Our experiments show that strong performance on general benchmarks does not transfer to professional scientific workflows, and that this gap is not a visual-grounding problem alone: failures arise from domain-specific operational knowledge, sparse pretraining coverage of scientific software, weak cross-tool artifact handoff, and critical states exposed only visually. Even the best model reaches only 25% success rate on GUI tasks and 45% on code tasks. MatToolBench therefore serves as a challenging diagnostic benchmark and real-environment testbed for data-scarce, knowledge-intensive scientific workflows.

segments.speaker: John
segments.en: Imagine a graduate course called Scientific Agents and Materials Workflows. Today's lecture is on MatToolBench: Benchmarking Multimodal Agents in Real-World Materials Science Workflows. As computer-use research expands, O-S-World 2.0 studies long-horizon desktop tasks, while ScienceBoard examines realistic scientific workflows. This paper, from researchers including Shanghai Jiao Tong University and Suzhou Laboratory, brings those directions together in specialized materials software. The field is moving toward agents that act across real applications; this work asks whether they can do so reliably in science. I see Noah's hand—go ahead, Noah.
segments.zh: 想象有一门研究生课程，叫《科学智能体与材料工作流》。今天这节课讲的是MatToolBench：在真实材料科学工作流中对多模态智能体进行基准测试。随着计算机使用研究的不断扩展，O-S-World 2.0研究的是长时程桌面任务，而ScienceBoard考察的是现实中的科学工作流。这篇论文来自上海交通大学和苏州实验室等机构的研究人员，把这两个方向汇聚到了专业材料软件中。这个领域正朝着让智能体在真实应用中行动的方向发展；这项工作要问的是，它们能否在科学场景中可靠地做到这一点。我看到Noah举手了——Noah，请讲。

segments.speaker: Noah
segments.en: Hi Professor, is the core idea simply to test whether an agent can click through scientific software?
segments.zh: 教授您好，核心思路是不是就测试一下智能体能不能在科研软件里点来点去？

segments.speaker: John
segments.en: That is part of it, but the benchmark tests more than clicking. It asks whether an agent can carry out a meaningful workflow while preserving the scientific state and producing usable outputs. The distinction matters: an interface action can look plausible yet select the wrong data, apply an unsuitable operation, or save an artifact that another tool cannot use. The benchmark measures operational competence, not whether an analysis is scientifically valid.
segments.zh: 这是其中一部分，但这个基准测试的不只是点击操作。它要考察的是，智能体能否在执行一个有意义的流程时，保持科学状态并产出可用的输出。这个区别很重要：一个界面操作看起来可能合理，却选错了数据、用了不合适的操作，或者保存了另一个工具无法使用的产物。这个基准衡量的是操作能力，而不是分析在科学上是否成立。

segments.speaker: John
segments.en: MatToolBench contains 204 tasks across ten tools, spanning graphical applications, scientific plotting, database access, and materials-analysis programming. The tasks use authentic files, including X-ray diffraction patterns, X-ray photoelectron spectra, microscopy images, crystal structures, and simulation outputs. Some tasks stay within one program; eight mixed tasks require handoffs between tools. That variety makes the benchmark resemble actual research work more closely than a collection of isolated questions or simplified software demonstrations.
segments.zh: MatToolBench包含204个任务，覆盖十种工具，涉及图形应用、科学绘图、数据库访问和材料分析编程。这些任务用的是真实文件，包括X射线衍射图谱、X射线光电子能谱、显微图像、晶体结构和模拟输出。有些任务只在一个程序里完成；还有八个混合任务需要在不同工具之间切换。这种多样性让这个基准更接近真实的研究工作，而不是一堆孤立的问题或简化的软件演示。

segments.speaker: Noah
segments.en: Quick question: does the benchmark count a task as failed if an agent completes most of the workflow but misses the final save?
segments.zh: 快速问一下：如果智能体完成了大部分工作流，但最后没保存，这个基准会把任务算作失败吗？

segments.speaker: John
segments.en: It records partial progress as well as full completion. Each task has independently checkable criteria, such as opening a file, setting a parameter, exporting an artifact, and saving it in the right place. The normalized score reflects the weighted criteria completed, whereas success rate requires every criterion to pass. This is useful diagnostically: a partial score can reveal progress, while a failed final handoff still signals that the workflow was not completed.
segments.zh: 它既记录完整完成，也记录部分进展。每个任务都有可独立检查的标准，比如打开文件、设置参数、导出产物并保存到正确位置。归一化得分反映的是已完成标准的加权结果，而成功率则要求所有标准都通过。这在诊断上很有用：部分得分能揭示进展，而最终交接失败仍然说明整个工作流没有完成。

segments.speaker: John
segments.en: The experiments run in a reproducible Windows 11 virtual machine. For graphical tasks, agents see full screenshots and use mouse coordinates, keyboard input, clipboard operations, and window controls; they do not receive accessibility trees in the main evaluation. Code agents instead receive execution feedback. Final states are checked using methods such as file inspection, optical character recognition, pixel analysis, and output parsing, so the scoring connects visible actions to concrete results.
segments.zh: 实验在一个可复现的 Windows 11 虚拟机里运行。对于图形界面任务，智能体看到的是完整截图，通过鼠标坐标、键盘输入、剪贴板操作和窗口控制来操作，在主评估中不会拿到无障碍树。代码智能体则接收执行反馈。最终状态会通过文件检查、光学字符识别、像素分析和输出解析等方法来核验，因此评分能把可见操作和具体结果对应起来。

segments.speaker: Noah
segments.en: So you're saying the models can often make progress, but keeping every step correct is the bigger challenge?
segments.zh: 所以你的意思是，这些模型往往能取得一些进展，但真正的挑战在于每一步都保持正确？

segments.speaker: John
segments.en: Exactly. The best overall result, from G-P-T five point four, was a normalized score of 51.2% and a full success rate of 34.3%. Claude reached 33.8% success overall, while the highest average success rate on graphical tasks was 25%. This gap between partial score and full completion suggests that agents can satisfy intermediate requirements but struggle to maintain a correct state across dependent operations.
segments.zh: 确实如此。整体表现最好的是GPT五点四，归一化得分51.2%，完全成功率34.3%。Claude的整体成功率是33.8%，而图形任务上最高的平均成功率只有25%。部分得分和完全完成之间的这个差距说明，智能体可以满足中间步骤的要求，但很难在相互依赖的操作中始终保持正确的状态。

segments.speaker: John
segments.en: The domain differences are revealing. DigitalMicrograph was particularly difficult, with no model above 20% success, while Materials Studio also challenged agents. Code tasks were easier overall: G-P-T five point four reached 45% success, and its OPTIMADE tasks reached as high as 85%. OriginPro separated models sharply: G-P-T five point four achieved 68.8% success, but several other models rarely completed those combined interface-and-scripting tasks.
segments.zh: 领域差异很能说明问题。DigitalMicrograph 特别难，没有任何模型成功率超过 20%，Materials Studio 也让智能体很头疼。代码类任务整体上更容易：GPT-5.4 达到了 45% 的成功率，它的 OPTIMADE 任务成功率甚至高达 85%。OriginPro 则把各模型明显拉开了差距：GPT-5.4 达到了 68.8% 的成功率，但其他好几个模型几乎完不成那些界面操作加脚本编写的组合任务。

segments.speaker: Noah
segments.en: Can you clarify why brief workflow hints make such a noticeable difference?
segments.zh: 你能解释一下，为什么简短的工作流程提示会带来这么明显的差别吗？

segments.speaker: John
segments.en: Professional software often contains conventions that are poorly represented in general training data. In ablations, removing hints reduced Doubao's JADE success from 25% to 5%, and its DigitalMicrograph success from 20% to zero. Removing guidance also erased G-P-T five point four's Materials Project successes. In OriginPro, script templates and workflow hints helped agents avoid GUI-only attempts that produced incorrect axes, missing annotations, or no saved output.
segments.zh: 专业软件里往往有一些约定俗成的用法，而通用训练数据很少能覆盖到。在消融实验中，去掉提示后，豆包的 JADE 成功率从 25% 掉到 5%，DigitalMicrograph 的成功率从 20% 直接归零。去掉引导后，GPT-5.4 在 Materials Project 上的成功也全部消失。在 OriginPro 里，脚本模板和工作流提示帮智能体避免了那些只能靠图形界面硬试的做法——那些做法会导致坐标轴错误、标注缺失，或者干脆什么都没保存下来。

segments.speaker: John
segments.en: A practical example is an agent transferring a spectrum from one application to another. It may perform the analysis correctly but export to the wrong path, choose an unusable extension, or save content that the next program cannot read. The mixed tasks expose this boundary problem. They also show why success cannot be judged solely by whether each program appeared to respond: the artifact must remain correct and usable throughout the workflow.
segments.zh: 一个实际的例子是，智能体把光谱数据从一个应用传到另一个应用。它可能分析做得没错，但导出到了错误的路径，选了没法用的扩展名，或者保存的内容下一个程序根本读不了。这些混合任务正好暴露了这个边界问题。它们也说明，为什么不能只看每个程序表面上有没有响应来判断成功：在整个工作流中，产物必须始终保持正确、可用。

segments.speaker: Noah
segments.en: How does this relate to ScienceBoard and general desktop benchmarks such as O-S-World 2.0?
segments.zh: 这和ScienceBoard以及O-S-World 2.0这类通用桌面基准有什么关系？

segments.speaker: John
segments.en: Those benchmarks help establish the broader direction: agents are being tested in longer, more realistic settings, including scientific work and desktop interaction. MatToolBench adds a domain-specific stress test, where legacy interfaces, scientific conventions, APIs, and file handoffs all matter together. The comparisons are informative, not controlled head-to-head experiments, because the tasks, observations, and scoring differ. The contribution is therefore a focused evaluation of challenges that general desktop scores may not capture.
segments.zh: 这些基准有助于确立更宏观的方向：智能体正在更长、更贴近真实的场景中接受测试，包括科研工作和桌面交互。MatToolBench 增加了一个领域特定的压力测试，其中遗留界面、科学惯例、API 和文件交接共同发挥作用。这些比较具有参考价值，但并非受控的正面对比实验，因为任务、观测和评分方式各不相同。因此，其贡献在于对通用桌面得分可能无法捕捉的挑战进行了有针对性的评估。

segments.speaker: Noah
segments.en: Hold on, does success here show that an agent's materials analysis is scientifically trustworthy?
segments.zh: 等等，这里的成功是否就说明智能体的材料分析在科学上是可信的？

segments.speaker: John
segments.en: No, and that limitation is essential. The benchmark checks whether tasks and outputs meet specified criteria; it does not establish that a chosen setting or interpretation is scientifically sound. It also covers ten tools, English instructions, and sessions limited to 50 steps, while some visual checks can vary with rendering. Future work could broaden tool coverage and add workflow memory, tutorial retrieval, API-version awareness, and stronger verification, while keeping human review in the loop.
segments.zh: 不，而且这个局限很关键。这个基准检验的是任务和输出是否满足既定标准，并不能证明所选的设置或解释在科学上是可靠的。它还只覆盖了十种工具、英文指令，以及限制在50步以内的会话，而有些视觉检查还会因渲染方式不同而变化。未来的工作可以扩大工具覆盖范围，并加入工作流记忆、教程检索、API版本感知和更强的验证，同时始终保留人工审核。

segments.speaker: John
segments.en: The central takeaway is that scientific agents need more than visual recognition or fluent code generation. They must understand software-specific procedures, verify intermediate states, and preserve artifacts across tools. MatToolBench makes those requirements measurable through realistic tasks and partial-credit diagnostics, while also showing how far current systems remain from dependable end-to-end workflows. Its results offer researchers a map of concrete failure points, not a certificate of scientific correctness. Thanks for listening. If you have any further questions, ask our AI assistant or drop a comment.
segments.zh: 核心结论是，科学智能体需要的远不止视觉识别或流畅的代码生成。它们必须理解特定软件的操作流程、验证中间状态，并在不同工具之间保留产物。MatToolBench 通过贴近真实的任务和部分得分诊断，让这些要求变得可衡量，同时也展示了当前系统距离可靠的端到端工作流还有多远。它的结果为研究者描绘了一张具体失败点的地图，而不是一张科学正确性的证书。感谢收听。如果还有更多问题，可以询问我们的 AI 助手，或者留言评论。
